_notes: Static reference data for the period-tracking module. These are commonly reported patterns from general research on the menstrual cycle, presented for education — not a diagnosis of any individual's experience, which can vary widely. Day ranges assume a typical ~28-day cycle and shift proportionally for longer/shorter cycles.

phases.hormoneNotes: Estrogen and progesterone are at their lowest point, triggering the uterine lining to shed. FSH begins rising late in this phase to recruit the next batch of follicles.
phases.moodEnergyNotes: Lower energy and a more introspective or withdrawn mood are commonly reported, alongside cramping, fatigue, and sometimes headaches — often attributed to the hormone low point and prostaglandin release.

nutritionFocus.why: replaces iron lost through menstrual bleeding
commonly suggested to help ease cramping
often reported to help with cramp discomfort

phases.dayRange: ~Days 1-13 (overlaps with menstrual phase, extends to ovulation)
phases.hormoneNotes: Estrogen rises steadily as FSH stimulates follicle growth in the ovaries.
phases.moodEnergyNotes: Rising energy, improved mood, and sharper mental clarity/motivation are commonly reported as estrogen climbs.

nutritionFocus.why: supports the higher activity/energy commonly felt in this phase
supports gut health, which plays a role in estrogen metabolism

phases.dayRange: ~Day 14 (varies; the day itself and 2-3 days prior are the most fertile window)
phases.hormoneNotes: A surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg; estrogen peaks just before this surge.
phases.moodEnergyNotes: Peak energy, sociability, and libido are commonly reported around this point in the cycle.

nutritionFocus.why: supports clearing excess estrogen at its peak
supports the slightly higher metabolic rate around ovulation

phases.hormoneNotes: Progesterone rises to prepare the uterine lining, then both progesterone and estrogen fall sharply in the final days if pregnancy doesn't occur — this drop is commonly linked to PMS symptoms.
phases.moodEnergyNotes: Energy often dips in the later part of this phase; irritability, low mood, food cravings, bloating, and breast tenderness (PMS) are commonly reported as hormone levels fall.

nutritionFocus.why: commonly reported to help stabilize mood and cravings
some research links adequate calcium intake to reduced PMS symptoms
commonly suggested to support mood regulation in this phase
often reported to worsen bloating and mood swings in this phase
